claim.pdf_says: 8.8.4.10.2 General format — the figure prints 'NOT condition-1' with NOT UNDERLINED (verified by cropping the 300 dpi render at x=320..720, y=620..700: a clear rule sits under N-O-T and stops before 'condition-1').
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10048 — 'NOT condition-1' (plain text; no <u> markup, no other required-word marker).
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is the standard's marker for a REQUIRED word (5.2.6). The transcription already has a convention for it and uses it correctly two figures earlier on page 229 ('data-name-1 IS [ <u>NOT</u> ] <u>OMITTED</u>'), so the marker was silently dropped here rather than deliberately omitted. A reader or generator that treats unmarked figure words as optional/user-supplied would mis-classify the negated-condition keyword.

verdict.reasoning: Both sides independently verified; every refutation route failed. (1) PDF side CONFIRMED by my own crop, not by trusting the claim: cropping E:/Temp/specrecon/v231/spec_p231.png at (300,620)-(750,700) and upscaling 3x shows the glyph sequence N-O-T with a single horizontal rule running beneath all three letters and terminating in the inter-word gap before 'c'; 'condition-1' carries no rule. So the printed figure is <underlined>NOT</underlined> condition-1. (2) Markdown side CONFIRMED verbatim: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 10048 is exactly 'NOT condition-1' — no <u>, no backticks, no bold, and no compensating prose note anywhere in the 8.8.4.10.2 block (heading L10046, blank L10047, content L10048, next anchor L10050). (3) 'Text is merely reflowed / present on an adjacent line' — REFUTED: the word NOT is present, but the required-word MARKING is absent, and nothing on page 231 records it. (4) 'Formatting only, no meaning change' — REFUTED by the standard's own notation clauses, which I read rather than assumed: 5.2.2 Keywords (L2628) 'shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required...'; 5.2.3 Optional words (L2641) 'shown in uppercase and NOT underlined in general formats. They MAY be written to add clarity.' Underlining is therefore a normative notation, not typography: as transcribed, the figure classifies NOT as an OPTIONAL word, which would make bare 'condition-1' a legal writing of a negated condition — the exact inversion of the construct's meaning. (5) 'Deliberate house style' — REFUTED locally: the transcription owns two working conventions for this and both are alive within a few lines. Inline markup is used on the identical word NOT at 8.8.4.3.2 L9691 '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1' and at 8.8.4.8.2 L9984 'data-name-1 IS [ <u>NOT</u> ] <u>OMITTED</u>' (L9984 does sit under the <a id="page-229"> anchor at L9952, so the claim's page attribution checks out). A prose 'Figure notes' convention is used on the very NEXT figure on this same page 231 (L10071: 'AND, OR, EXCLUSIVE-OR, and XOR are underlined in the printed standard (required words)'), and again at 8.8.4.7.2 L9912 and 8.8.4.12.2 L10137. Page 231 thus applies the compensating convention to its second figure and applies neither convention to its first — internally inconsistent on a single page. (6) 'Claim misquotes a source' — the only misquote is the clause number: the required/optional-word notation is 5.2.2 and 5.2.3, not 5.2.6 (5.2.6 is Options, i.e. brackets and braces). That is a citation slip in the rationale, not an error in the finding. Genuine content discrepancy: the printed figure marks NOT as a keyword; the transcription does not, and under the standard's own notation an unmarked uppercase word means something different.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED with two corrections to the framing. (a) Clause citation: the marker's meaning is fixed by 5.2.2 Keywords ('uppercase and underlined ... required') and 5.2.3 Optional words ('uppercase and NOT underlined ... may be written'), not by 5.2.6 (Options / brackets and braces). (b) Scope: this is NOT a page-231-local slip. A sweep of all 281 'General format' sections shows 154 with non-fenced bodies, of which 92 carry no underline markup at all — including siblings that print underlines in the PDF, e.g. 7.3.8.4.2 L3878 'compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED' and most of the 15.x FUNCTION formats. So p231 L10048 is one instance of a document-wide systemic loss of the keyword underline, and any fix should be swept across that population rather than patched at this line. What IS locally damning, and what makes the finding worth keeping at page 231, is the intra-page inconsistency: the second figure on the same page (8.8.4.11.2, L10063-L10071) preserves its underlines via a prose 'Figure notes' block, while the first figure gets neither that note nor the inline <u> markup that the same transcription applies to the identical word NOT at L9691 and L9984. Severity 'cosmetic' is right for a human reader — 8.8.4.10.1 states in prose that a condition is negated 'by use of the logical operator NOT' — but it is meaning-bearing for any mechanical consumer that derives required-vs-optional word status from the figure.
